newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Leaving bloc for dust.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Leaving bloc for dust.

text.p: Australian bonds put in yet another strong performance against the dollar bloc after a weak set of retail trade data for April, fuelling speculation that the Reserve Bank's easing cycle is not yet over.
Retail trade slumped 1.7 percent when a small 0.5 percent rise was expected, and was the first back-to-back fall for nearly four years.
The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread sank to its lowest level in some three years to around 70 basis points, and the three-year spread went even further negative.

U.S. Treasuries firmed on Thursday on foreign buying and after a positive response to a five-year note sale and firmed further in Tokyo. The market faces a clutch of data on Friday, including the second estimate of first quarter GDP,

The market also outpaced the Canadian market, which rallied on Thursday, finding relief from a rise in its currency, having being dogged by fears of a Fed rate cut in recent days and ahead of next week's election.
The spread tightening was less notable against New Zealand, which jumped on board the local rally.
